comment: The principles emphasize technical and institutional properties, but omit several principles central to HISP’s socio-technical approach: participatory co-design, use of information for action, incremental learning, local ownership and accessible grievance/redress. HISP describes action research, local–global feedback and long-term capacity building as core to sustainable systems: https://dhis2.org/hisp-approach These principles also align with the principles of digital developmen, e.g. "design with people, share reuse and improve"

public.text: The principles emphasize technical and institutional properties, but omit several principles central to HISP’s socio-technical approach: participatory co-design, use of information for action, incremental learning, local ownership and accessible grievance/redress. HISP describes action research, local–global feedback and long-term capacity building as core to sustainable systems: https://dhis2.org/hisp-approach These principles also align with the principles of digital developmen, e.g. "design with people, share reuse and improve"
public.suggestedRevision: Add a principle titled ‘Participation, learning and local ownership’. Require meaningful involvement of health workers, managers, communities and subnational authorities throughout the lifecycle; iterative learning from use; feedback to data producers; locally accountable stewardship; and accessible mechanisms to correct data and challenge harmful decisions.
